understanding.purpose: A reference for identifying mathematical symbols, their names, LaTeX commands, and meanings.
understanding.reading: Readers can scan the symbol or name to find an entry, then read across the row to copy its LaTeX command or understand its meaning. The longer meanings will determine most row heights.
groups: Symbol and Name work together to identify each notation.
LaTeX is a compact, copyable representation of the symbol.
Meaning contains explanatory prose and needs most of the available width.
keep_intact: Individual words and the column headers
may_wrap: Meaning prose can wrap naturally across lines.
Multiword names such as Tensor product can wrap when the corresponding meaning already makes the row taller.

bad.why: The narrow Meaning column would turn each explanation into a tall block while leaving much of the available viewport unused, making comparisons across rows slower.

contrast.why: The narrow Meaning column would turn each explanation into a tall block while leaving much of the available viewport unused, making comparisons across rows slower.

final.rationale: The preferred designs keep every name, symbol and LaTeX command on one line, making the three reference columns easy to scan together. Meaning receives most of the width and fits each explanation within three lines, giving the rows a steady rhythm. The three preferred designs have identical widths and renderings.

general: Give identifying columns enough room to keep labels and codes intact when readers need to scan them quickly.
Allocate width according to content and reading purpose; prose usually needs more room than short identifiers.
Judge wrapping by its effect on scanning and row rhythm, not by table height alone.
specific: A 126px Name column keeps 'Tensor product' on one line.
At 433px, Meaning wraps the tensor-product explanation to four lines; at 438px it fits in three.
The Symbol and LaTeX columns are already at the stated minimum widths needed to fit their longest unbreakable content.

final.tradeoffs: Narrowing Name gives Meaning more room, but wraps 'Tensor product'; widening Name to 131px keeps that label intact while creating a fourth line in its explanation. Both remain publishable, though the preferred balance keeps the label intact and maintains the more even row rhythm.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative: only the preferred width combination is verified as equally good in the supplied renders. Nearby widths could work as well, but their line breaks have not been shown.

A.why: The compact identifier columns give the meanings comfortable three-line blocks, though Tensor product wraps across two lines.

B.why: Equal column widths leave large empty areas beside a severely narrow Meaning column, creating tall rows and making comparisons harder.

C.why: The meanings read in balanced three-line blocks and the identifiers stay intact, but Tensor product wraps in the narrow Name column.

D.why: Names and LaTeX entries stay on one line, but the narrow Meaning column creates tall rows while substantial viewport space remains unused.

E.why: The meanings have a comfortable width and consistent row heights, but Tensor product still wraps despite the wider Name column.

F.why: All names and LaTeX entries stay intact, while the Meaning column remains wide enough for readable three-line descriptions and consistent rows.

reviews.unsure: A, C, and E are close in overall rhythm; their relative order is a matter of preference for the particular line breaks.

A.why: The meaning column has comfortable line lengths and the identifiers remain intact, though “Tensor product” wraps despite nearby alternatives fitting it on one line.

B.why: All names and LaTeX commands stay on one line, while the meaning column has enough room for readable, consistent three-line entries.

C.why: Equal column widths leave excessive blank space around short identifiers and squeeze meanings into narrow, heavily wrapped passages, making rows difficult to scan.

D.why: The wide meaning column reads comfortably and commands stay intact, but “Tensor product” wraps and the name column feels tight.

E.why: Names and commands remain intact, but the unused viewport space leaves meanings in a narrow column with frequent wrapping and tall rows.

F.why: Meanings have generous, readable space and commands stay intact, but “Tensor product” wraps where a slightly wider name column would keep it together.

reviews.unsure: A, D and F are close in overall readability; the value of keeping “Tensor product” on one line is a matter of typographic judgment.
